target_customer: Manufacturers and cargo owners in Africa, with truck operators as the supply side
problem: Freight in Nigeria and Africa was fragmented, with trucks idle and cargo owners unable to find reliable capacity.
business_model: Freight marketplace taking a commission per trip, reported at 15 percent, later with fleet management services
product_category: Digital freight marketplace and logistics operating system

founders.name: Obi Ozor
founders.background_notes: Named a co-founder by Disrupt Africa and a founder by TechCrunch. Later became Enugu State transportation commissioner and bought the company back in 2025 per TechCabal reporting. No education found.

founders.name: Ife Oyedele
founders.background_notes: Named on the YC page as Ife Oyedele II; reported as leaving in 2021 to pursue other interests.

investors: Fund for Export Development in Africa

exit.reason: Investors sold their stakes to co-founder Obi Ozor who took on the debt, reported at about 10 billion naira, after operations were largely paused in late 2024

competitors.name: Lori Systems
competitors.what: Kenyan trucking marketplace that expanded into Nigeria in September 2018

technical_complexity.rationale: A mobile marketplace with matching, tracking and payments across fragmented trucking, standard engineering with operational hard parts.

defensibility.rationale: Two sided supply of trucks and cargo gave some network effects, but drivers and shippers could multi-home.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent absorbed it; the company grew with Goldman Sachs and IFC backing, then contracted in 2024.

market_need_then: Nigerian freight was largely informal and fragmented, and the founder pitched an Uber for trucks; Lori Systems entering Nigeria in 2018 shows the demand was visible to competitors.

branding.domain_note: kobo360.com used as the main domain.

identity.voice_and_tone: Positioned in press as the Uber of trucks

branding.community_and_virality: Wide press coverage in African tech outlets and a YC and Goldman Sachs backing story; no merch or fan activity found.

brand_strength.rationale: Well known in African tech media and with multinationals, but no source documents the brand itself as a growth driver.

outcome_analysis: Kobo360 raised 1.2M pre-seed, 6M in December 2018, a 20M Series A in August 2019 and a reported 48M Series B in 2022, expanding to seven countries. In November 2024 it laid off staff and paused most operations, and in March 2025 investors sold to co-founder Obi Ozor who took on the debt. The failure factors are inferred from the layoffs and debt reporting rather than a company statement of cause.
notes: The 2019 total of 30M was 20M equity plus 10M bank working capital, recorded here as the 20M equity Series A; outlets differ on whether IFC, TLcom and YC were new or existing. The December 2018 round is labeled other because TechCrunch gives no stage label. The Series B of 48M dated 2022-09 rests on one database (startupintros citing TechCrunch); sources conflict (Wikipedia 56M, BounceWatch 2021-12, SignalBase 68M), so treat the amount as unverified. Company site returned 503. Lori Systems source is dated 2018-12, about five months after the S18 batch start; it is noted because TechCrunch quotes the founder naming Lori. The 2025 ownership change and debt come from TechCabal search snippets and the techcabal page returned 403, so details are secondhand. The exit type is unknown because no sale to an outside buyer occurred and the YC status is inactive.
